[01:28] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So you were paying twenty-one and a half thousand a year for what — two builders?
[01:34] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Two builders and eleven workflows, most of which are quite simple.
[01:40] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Did the workflows work?
[01:42] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): They worked perfectly. That's the frustrating part. I've got no complaint about the product at all.
[01:50] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then what are you moving to?
[01:53] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Zapier. Which we had before, which we should probably never have left.
[02:00] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What'll that cost?
[02:02] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): About two thousand a year. Maybe two and a half with the tier we need.
[02:08] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So a tenth.
[02:10] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): A tenth, yes.
[02:12] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Will it do everything?
[02:14] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [pause] No. We'll lose the approval steps and we'll lose the run history, which I'll genuinely miss. But nineteen thousand pounds is a member of staff for four months, and when I put it that way to my managing director, the conversation was quite short.
[02:34] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a hard argument to counter.
[02:37] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): It's an impossible argument to counter. And I'd like to say — I did think about it properly. I'm not being flippant. I sat down and listed what we'd lose.
[02:50] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What was on the list?
[02:52] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): The run history. The approval forms, because our contractor sign-off uses those and Zapier can't really do it. And the fact that when something breaks, I know within an hour rather than when a tenant rings up.
[03:09] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Those are the three things that matter.
[03:12] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): They're the three things that matter and they're worth something. They're not worth nineteen thousand pounds a year to a company our size.
[03:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Alastair, do you want to come in?
[03:25] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Yeah — Hazel, I mean, I'm sorry it's ended up here. Is there — I mean, is there a version where we look at the pricing? Because I could go and —
[03:37] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Alastair, no. I'm not doing that.
[03:41] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No, I understand, I just —
[03:44] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): If you can do it for eight thousand now, that tells me you could have done it for eight thousand two years ago, and then I'd be quite cross.
[03:54] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [pause] That's fair.
[03:57] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Hazel, can I ask about the original purchase?
[04:01] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): You can, and Alastair may not enjoy it.
[04:05] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's fine. Honestly.
[04:08] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): When we bought this, I was told it would scale with us. That we'd start with the fault-reporting workflow and then do compliance, and then service charges, and then contractor management. And that was true — it would have. But we never did any of it.
[04:28] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Why not?
[04:30] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Because we're two hundred and forty people and everyone's already got a job. The roadmap I agreed to in the sales process assumed a version of Oakhill that spent time on process improvement, and we've never once had that time.
[04:47] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Was that discussed?
[04:49] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): It was discussed enthusiastically.
[04:52] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] By whom?
[04:55] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): By both of us, to be fair. I was enthusiastic too. I'm not putting this all on Alastair.
[05:03] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I did — I mean, I remember that conversation and you were quite keen on the compliance one.
[05:11] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): I was extremely keen on the compliance one. I've been keen on the compliance one for three years. It has never once reached the top of my list.
[05:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So the purchase was priced against a future that didn't happen.
[05:27] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Yes. That's a good way of putting it. We paid for eleven workflows' worth of value and a plan for forty.
[05:37] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Is there anything we could have done?
[05:40] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [pause] Yes, actually. Two things.
[05:44] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Go on.
[05:46] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Someone should have noticed after six months that we had four users on a thirty-user plan and said something. Not sold me something. Said something.
[05:58] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a fair criticism. We look at that data.
[06:03] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Do you?
[06:04] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): We look at it. Whether anyone acts on it for an account your size is a different question, and the answer is usually no.
[06:14] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): At least you're honest.
[06:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What's the second thing?
[06:19] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): There should be a smaller plan. Something for a company that needs five workflows and three users and doesn't need thirty seats. If you'd had something at five or six hundred a month I'd still be a customer and I'd probably have done the compliance one eventually.
[06:39] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): There isn't one.
[06:41] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): I know there isn't. Alastair told me at the time.
[06:45] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I did say that.
[06:47] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): You did say that, in fairness. You said the entry point is Growth and that's the entry point.
[06:54] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Did you consider not buying?
[06:57] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): I did. And I decided the fault-reporting problem was bad enough to justify it, which it was. For about a year.
[07:07] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What changed after a year?
[07:10] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Nothing changed. That's the thing. It kept working. But the pain it solved stopped being fresh, and the invoice kept arriving, and eventually somebody looks at a renewal and asks what this is for.
[07:26] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): The problem being solved becomes invisible.
[07:30] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): The problem being solved becomes invisible. Exactly that. Nobody remembers how bad it was.
[07:38] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Do you think you'll regret it?
[07:41] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [pause] Possibly. I think there'll be a moment in about four months when something breaks and nobody notices for two days and I'll think, well, that used to be handled.
[07:55] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And then?
[07:57] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): And then I'll deal with it, because that's a two-day problem and not a nineteen-thousand-pound problem.
[08:04] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a rational position.
[08:07] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): I've had a lot of time to think about it. I've been putting off this decision since May.
[08:14] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Can I ask about the last year of service? How was it?
[08:19] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Fine. Genuinely fine. I think I've raised two tickets in two years and both were answered.
[08:27] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Did anyone from us contact you?
[08:30] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): You did, in — March? An email about a new feature.
[08:36] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): A product announcement.
[08:38] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): A product announcement, yes.
[08:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's not contact.
[08:43] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): No, it isn't.
[08:45] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] I'm going to be direct with you. Your account was in a segment that doesn't get an assigned CSM. I'm on this call because it's a churn, not because I've been managing you.
[08:59] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): I'd worked that out. You've been very good today but you clearly hadn't heard of us before Tuesday.
[09:07] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Monday, actually.
[09:09] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [laughs] Monday.
[09:12] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'm not going to pretend otherwise.
[09:15] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): I don't mind. It's a commercial reality. But it does rather answer the question of why nobody noticed the four users.
[09:25] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It does.
[09:27] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I say something?
[09:29] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Go on.
[09:31] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I think — looking back, I probably should have pushed harder on whether you had the capacity for the roadmap we talked about. I was excited about it and you were excited about it and neither of us asked who was actually going to do it.
[09:49] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [pause] That's a good thing to say.
[09:53] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I've been thinking about it since Ruth sent me the notice.
[09:58] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): For what it's worth, Alastair, I don't think you did anything wrong. You sold me a good product that does what it says. I just bought more of it than I needed.
[10:10] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thanks. I appreciate that.
[10:13] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Practical things. What do you need for the exit?
[10:18] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Our workflow definitions, if only so I know how to rebuild them in Zapier.
[10:24] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): You can export those through the API. I'll send instructions — and honestly, for eleven simple workflows, screenshots might be more useful than the JSON.
[10:36] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Screenshots would be much more useful.
[10:39] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then I'll get someone to produce those. It's not a thing we offer, but it's eleven workflows and it'll take an hour.
[10:48] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): That's kind.
[10:50] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What about run history?
[10:52] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Do I need it?
[10:54] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): You tell me. Is there any compliance reason you'd need to show what happened to a fault report from eighteen months ago?
[11:03] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [pause] Possibly, actually. There's a Building Safety Act angle on fault response times.
[11:11] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then take the export. It's better to have it and not need it.
[11:16] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): How do I get it?
[11:18] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Run events API. I'll send the pagination details, because two years of records will hit a limit and you'll assume it's broken.
[11:28] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): I definitely would have assumed that.
[11:31] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Everyone does. And I'll arrange a deletion confirmation for afterwards with an actual date on it.
[11:39] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Thank you.
[11:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Your contract ends the eleventh of November. Do you want read-only access past that?
[11:47] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Two weeks would help. We'll be running both in parallel through October.
[11:53] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'll give you until the end of November. No charge.
[11:58] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): That's generous.
[12:00] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's not generous, it's just not petty.
[12:03] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [laughs] Some vendors are petty.
[12:07] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Some vendors are very petty.
[12:10] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): One last question. If we did have a smaller plan — five hundred a month, five workflows, three users, no approval forms — would you buy it?
[12:22] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [pause] With the approval forms, yes. Without them, no, because that's the bit Zapier can't do and it's the only thing I'll actually miss.
[12:34] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So approval forms are the feature.
[12:37] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): For a company like us, the approval forms and the run history are the whole product. The rest is capability I'll never reach.
[12:47] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's genuinely useful and I'll pass it on.
[12:51] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Will anything happen?
[12:53] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Probably not. But it'll be one more data point and eventually someone counts them.
[13:00] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [laughs] That's the most realistic thing anyone's said to me all week.
[13:06] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Thank you, Hazel. Genuinely.
[13:09] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Thanks both. Alastair — no hard feelings.
[13:14] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): None at all. Good luck with the compliance one.
[13:18] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [laughs] It'll never happen. Bye.

answer.summary: Both customers left because the product fit their needs and operating model poorly, not because it simply failed. Verity Payments said the core problem was that operations never actually built workflows and the platform became an engineering tool; Oakhill Property said they overbought a costly plan for a small automation need and would rather use cheaper Zapier, keeping only features like approval forms and run history. In both calls, they also said better onboarding, the right role/person to own workflows, and more realistic pricing or scoping might have changed the outcome.

question: What is different about how the sales team handles renewals versus new business?
correct_reason: The overall contrast between renewals and new business is right, but the answer misses that the CSM leads renewals and misses the standard 7% uplift.

verdicts.reason: The answer says renewals open with usage and outcomes data, but it never says the CSM (Ruth) opens and runs them. It also doesn't cover the AE/CSM split or the Halberd case.
The answer describes new business as discovery-led (pain, mapping the process) with security raised early. It leaves out the AE+SE roles.
The answer mentions 'renewal uplift' only in general terms and never gives the standard 7% figure. It does mention run tiers, but not Pinewood's notice deadline.
The answer says exact figures are deferred while the user model is unclear.
The answer quotes 'we jointly write three to five pilot success criteria'. It does not mention 'don't buy' as a valid outcome.

WHOLE TRANSCRIPTS (shown in full, not as notes): CALL-011, CALL-012, CALL-013, CALL-016, CALL-017, CALL-018, CALL-019, CALL-020

=== CALL-001 (call kind: prospect)
CALL ID: CALL-001
DATE: 2026-06-03
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
PROSPECT: Acme Logistics
INDUSTRY: Logistics
COMPANY SIZE: 650 employees
STAGE: Discovery / first demo
DURATION: 30 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Maya Chen, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Jon Bell, Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow
- Rachel Morgan, VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics
- Tom Alvarez, Director of Customer Success, Acme Logistics
TRANSCRIPT
[01:01] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Right. Okay, so my plan for today, roughly — I want to spend the first chunk just understanding how you actually handle this, and then Jon can show the parts of the product that map onto that. Not the full tour. I'd rather skip the bits that aren't relevant.
[01:18] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): Please. I've sat through the full tour from three vendors this quarter.
[01:24] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Understood. So — where does it hurt?
[01:29] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): The short version is we've got too much operational work living between systems. And I want to be clear up front, we're not looking for another dashboard. We've got dashboards. We need something that actually moves work along and makes it visible who owns what.
[01:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can you give me a concrete one?
[01:51] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): Sure. Handoffs between sales, onboarding and customer success. All of that is managed through spreadsheets and Slack reminders. So renewal risks and implementation blockers get noticed late. Not never — late.
[02:09] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): How late is late?
[02:12] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): Depends. Sometimes a week. Sometimes we find out at the QBR, which is — yeah.
[02:20] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And is it that the steps are manual, or —
[...]
[04:38] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): Actually, can I do that? Because I have the same instinct. What does this cost? Roughly. I don't need a quote, I need to know whether we're in the same postcode.
[04:50] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Fair. Growth starts at eighteen hundred a month, that's up to thirty users, annual agreement. Enterprise is custom — that's where the governance and security capabilities sit, plus higher usage.
[...]
[05:31] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): I can probably still justify it if we replace enough manual work, and maybe some of what we're paying Gainsight for. But I'd need a clearer ROI story than "it saves time."
[...]
[09:18] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That's exactly the right level to test at, and it's the bit I'd want you to push on. Workflows are event-driven but each run holds state. So you can branch on data, pause for approvals, retry external actions, set timeout rules, and push an exception into a queue rather than just failing quietly.
[09:40] Tom Alvarez (Director of Customer Success, Acme Logistics): Can the queue be owned by a team? Not a named person. People change roles constantly here and individual ownership is genuinely one of the reasons our current stuff breaks.
[09:53] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Yes. Route to a group, resolve a person dynamically from a field, or use an on-call style fallback. And the run history persists, so an admin can see the inputs, which steps ran, where it stopped.
[10:08] Tom Alvarez (Director of Customer Success, Acme Logistics): Okay. That's better than what we've got.
[10:12] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): There's a second use case I'd flag, not for phase one — identifying renewal risk by combining CRM fields, support activity and product usage signals out of Snowflake. I don't need it now. I do want to know the architecture doesn't rule it out.
[10:31] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): It doesn't. Different shape of workflow — that's more scheduled and query-driven than event-driven — but same platform.
[...]
[14:19] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): One thing I noted from your pre-call form — you've got roughly a hundred and forty customer-facing users but you'd only expect twenty-five to actually build or administer workflows?
[...]
[20:05] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That's fine. Baseline is SOC 2 Type II. SAML SSO and SCIM on Enterprise. Encryption in transit and at rest. Audit logs cover administrative and workflow events. Retention configurable within supported ranges. EU residency available on Enterprise if you ever need it.
[20:27] Tom Alvarez (Director of Customer Success, Acme Logistics): Can you send the SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation?
[...]
[21:16] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I appreciate that, genuinely. We'll write it up as a pilot exit criterion. If we can't satisfy it, that should be an explicit result, not something that surfaces in procurement at the end.
[...]
[22:03] Tom Alvarez (Director of Customer Success, Acme Logistics): That separation would help. AI's interesting but it's not worth blocking the automation case over.
[22:11] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Right — pricing properly. What counts as a user, since you asked.
[22:17] Tom Alvarez (Director of Customer Success, Acme Logistics): Yes, because we may have a small number of builders and a lot of people who only approve something or receive a notification.
[22:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Builders and full workspace users are the licensed users. Approval-only or notification-only can be structured differently depending on the package. I'm deliberately not giving you an exact number today because without the user model any number I give you is misleading.
[22:46] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): Please make that explicit in the proposal. I do not want to find out in month four that every occasional approver needs a full seat.
[22:56] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It'll be itemised — assumed builder count, viewer and approver population, expected workflow volume, and any one-time services separately.
[...]
[23:52] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): For a pilot we can baseline one or two things before we automate — elapsed time, number of manual touches, exception rate, engineer hours spent maintaining the current process.
[...]
[24:26] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): I own the project. IT security and the VP of Customer Success sign off. Finance gets involved above twenty-five thousand a year, so — yes, finance gets involved. Operationally I'd expect a small central group owning standards, business teams contributing requirements.
[...]
[24:58] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That's more or less our recommended model. Start with a few centrally owned templates, define who can publish to production, separate dev from prod.
[25:10] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Timing — you'd said choose a vendor before end of July, first workflows live in September?
[...]
[25:29] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): One representative workflow working with real enough data. Security gates understood. A commercial model without hidden scaling surprises. And the people who'll operate it have to believe they can own it — that last one is not a small thing.
[...]
[25:57] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Agreed. We can define the pilot against the status quo and the alternative. And a perfectly valid outcome is "don't buy OrbitFlow" if the existing approach meets the criteria more cheaply.
[...]
[26:17] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): Fair enough. Look — my read is I'm interested enough to test it. If you can give us a sandbox I can supply three real workflows and we'll see whether the exception handling is as good as it looked today.
[26:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's exactly what I'd want. So — we send the security pack and a short architecture summary, you send the representative workflow and sample data, and we jointly write three to five pilot success criteria. Then we decide on the sandbox.
[...]
[28:05] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let me summarise what I heard, and correct me. You don't need automation for its own sake. The opportunity is making a small number of cross-system processes observable, easier to change, and less dependent on specific individuals. The pilot has to prove integration reliability, exception handling, governance, and that there's a credible operating model on your side.
[...]
[28:39] Tom Alvarez (Director of Customer Success, Acme Logistics): Can you also write down the assumptions you made today? Some of what we told you was approximate and I don't want it hardening into requirements by accident.
[28:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Will do. Written recap with open questions separated from confirmed requirements.

=== CALL-002 (call kind: prospect)
CALL ID: CALL-002
DATE: 2026-06-05
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
PROSPECT: BrightPath Health
INDUSTRY: Digital health
COMPANY SIZE: 1,100 employees
STAGE: Technical discovery
DURATION: 34 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Maya Chen, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Jon Bell, Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow
- Priya Shah, Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health
- Elliot Greene, Security Architect, BrightPath Health
TRANSCRIPT
[00:00] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Morning both. Priya, Elliot — thanks for the time.
[00:05] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): Morning. Quick logistics thing before we start. Elliot has a hard stop at forty past. So can we do security first and everything else after he drops?
[00:17] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Absolutely, and honestly that's the right order anyway. If security's a no, the rest is theatre.
[00:25] Elliot Greene (Security Architect, BrightPath Health): I appreciate you saying that. Most vendors want to do the demo first and then act surprised.
[00:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I've been on the wrong end of that. Okay — Elliot, you drive. What's on your list?
[00:41] Elliot Greene (Security Architect, BrightPath Health): Right. The list is: we need to resolve the BAA question, review your subprocessors, SSO and SCIM, understand retention, and confirm how US data is handled.
[00:57] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which of those is the gate?
[01:01] Elliot Greene (Security Architect, BrightPath Health): The BAA is the gate. If you can't offer one, we cannot use OrbitFlow for any workflow that may involve protected health information. That's not me being difficult, that's — that's just where we are.
[01:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Understood, and I want to be careful here because this is exactly the thing people fudge on sales calls. I'm not going to give you a yes on this call. What I will do is get you a written answer from our legal and compliance side within — Jon, what's realistic, a week?
[...]
[06:31] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What else can we send? SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation — is that the pack?
[06:42] Elliot Greene (Security Architect, BrightPath Health): Add pen test summary. And yes. And we'll send you our questionnaire, which is long, and I apologise in advance.
[...]
[11:36] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And you've got Power Automate today.
[11:40] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): We do. It's already covered by our Microsoft agreement, which matters a lot to procurement.
[...]
[12:15] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the right question, and we won't try to replace everything. Plenty of customers keep an iPaaS or internal services for deep integration and use us for business-owned workflows — the ones with human decisions, exceptions, cross-functional handoffs.
[12:35] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): That's closer to how we'd think about it. I'd be nervous if the proposal was migrate everything off Microsoft.
[12:44] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It isn't, and frankly that proposal would lose to your licensing agreement anyway.
[...]
[12:54] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let me try a phase-one candidate on you. Route implementation requests from HubSpot into Jira, enrich them with account data, notify Teams, track exceptions — and do all of that without copying sensitive notes into three more systems.
[...]
[15:56] Elliot Greene (Security Architect, BrightPath Health): The idea is to give operations teams a governed way to build simple workflows without receiving broad access to production systems. I'm supportive of that in principle. In practice it lives or dies on whether the permission model is genuinely least-privilege or just a UI that hides things.
[16:20] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That's a fair challenge and I'd want to demo the permission model specifically rather than hand-wave it.
[16:29] Elliot Greene (Security Architect, BrightPath Health): Then let's do that in the next session. Right — I have to go. Priya, you've got my notes. Thanks both.
[16:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thanks Elliot, appreciate the directness.
[...]
[17:36] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Took us nine days to find. And the reason it took nine days is the exact thing you described — we could see that something was wrong downstream, we could not see which step, when, or how often. That's genuinely why I care about run history more than I care about the connector catalogue.
[...]
[21:40] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): We cache metadata but refresh it, and mapping errors surface on the run. For high-impact flows I'd recommend explicit validation at the start rather than assuming every source field is populated. You can also alert when error rates cross a threshold.
[22:00] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): I'd want that in the evaluation. A demo with clean data proves nothing.
[...]
[22:55] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): For your stack it's a mix of native connectors and API-based options. In a pilot I'd want to validate each required operation rather than pointing at a logo on our integrations page.
[...]
[23:53] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Growth starts at eighteen hundred a month for up to thirty users on an annual agreement. Enterprise is custom-priced — that's where advanced governance, the security capabilities, and higher usage sit. Given your list, you're an Enterprise conversation, not a Growth one.
[24:15] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): Honestly? I'm not ready to react to that.
[...]
[24:22] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): I don't mean that as a negotiating position. Procurement will not have a serious pricing conversation until security tells us whether the BAA requirement can be met. If the answer's no, the price is irrelevant.
[24:38] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's completely logical and I'm not going to push. What I'd ask is that when we do get to it, you let me build the model around your actual user population rather than a headline number.
[24:53] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): What counts as a user? Because we'd have a small number of builders and a lot of people who only approve something or get a notification.
[25:04] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Builders and full workspace users are the licensed ones. Approval-only or notification-only can be structured differently depending on package. I'm deliberately not quoting you a figure today because without the user model any figure I give is misleading.
[25:23] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): Please make that explicit in the proposal when it comes. I don't want to discover in month four that every occasional approver needs a full seat.
[25:35] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It'll be itemised. Assumed builders, viewer and approver population, expected workflow volume, one-time services separately.
[25:46] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): Thank you.
[25:49] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): How would you make the ROI case internally? Headcount, cycle time, errors, engineering maintenance?
[25:58] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): Not headcount. I wouldn't sell it that way and it also isn't true. The stronger case is consistency and speed. We've got expensive people doing coordination work because the systems don't carry enough process context. And there's the backlog cost, which is harder to quantify but it's real — eleven weeks of waiting has a number attached to it somewhere.
[26:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): For a pilot we can baseline one or two things before automating. Elapsed time, manual touches, exception rate, or systems-group hours spent on requests.
[...]
[26:48] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): I'd also measure adoption. A technically correct workflow that everyone routes around is a failed implementation. That's literally what happened with our last internal tool.
[...]
[27:07] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): I'm the sponsor — business systems. Security can veto, as you've seen. Privacy counsel reviews the DPA and the BAA. Procurement handles final terms.
[27:22] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Four gates.
[27:24] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): Four gates. Welcome to healthcare.
[...]
[27:31] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): A small central group owning standards, business teams contributing requirements. With naming conventions, change control on the important ones, and a rule that someone other than the creator can understand each production flow.
[27:48] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That matches what we recommend. A few centrally owned templates, defined publishing rights, dev separated from prod.
[...]
[28:32] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): No production launch before Q4. That's firm. But we could run a non-sensitive proof of concept in August — synthetic data, or clearly non-PHI.
[...]
[28:53] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): One representative workflow working with real enough data. The security gates understood, and by understood I mean answered. A commercial model without hidden scaling surprises. And the people who'd operate it believing they can own it.
[...]
[29:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then let's define the pilot against the status quo and against Power Automate. And I'll say the same thing I said to Elliot — a valid outcome is "don't buy OrbitFlow" if the existing approach meets the criteria more cheaply.
[...]
[29:50] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): So — where does that leave us. My read is I would still consider a limited pilot with synthetic or clearly non-PHI data. But I want to be explicit about something: a successful pilot would not automatically mean we can deploy broadly. Those are two different decisions and they have different approvers.
[...]
[30:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Concrete next steps then. We send the security pack — SOC 2, subprocessors, DPA, architecture diagram, retention docs, pen test summary. Separately, and this is the one that matters, a written position on the BAA within a week. You send us the representative workflow and some sample data, ideally messy. And we jointly write three to five pilot success criteria.
[30:53] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): And a session on the permission model for Elliot.
[...]
[31:04] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Yeah. I'd want an hour and I'd want Elliot to bring his worst-case scenario rather than me showing him a clean one.
[...]
[31:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let me summarise. You don't need automation for its own sake. The opportunity is a systems group that builds components rather than fulfilling tickets, and a small number of cross-system processes that are observable and less dependent on individuals. The blocker is regulatory, not technical, and until it's answered nothing else moves.
[...]
[32:04] Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems, BrightPath Health): You want me to do that?
[32:07] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No, sorry — I'll do that. I'll send a recap with open questions separated from confirmed requirements.

=== CALL-003 (call kind: prospect)
CALL ID: CALL-003
DATE: 2026-06-11
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
PROSPECT: Cedar & Finch
INDUSTRY: E-commerce
COMPANY SIZE: 180 employees
STAGE: Discovery / demo
DURATION: 17 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Leo Grant, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Sophie Reed, Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch
- Marcus Lee, Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch
TRANSCRIPT
[00:09] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Yeah, sorry, I'm walking. I'll be at a desk in five.
[00:14] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No problem. So normally I'd spend twenty minutes on discovery before showing anything, but —
[...]
[00:25] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): We've done three of these in a fortnight. I can recite our own pain points. Can we just see it and I'll interrupt when something matters?
[00:35] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Deal. I'll ask about four questions along the way rather than up front. Fair?
[...]
[00:43] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): One thing before I share — I'm on my own today. Nina, our solutions engineer, is with another customer. So if you ask me something properly technical I'm going to say "I'll come back to you" rather than make it up.
[...]
[03:50] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Yes — you can alert when error rates cross a threshold. And that's the right instinct, everyone who alerts per-failure ends up ignoring all of them.
[...]
[05:07] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Understood. I'm going to be careful here — I believe the Shopify integration is native and event-driven, but I'm not going to swear to the exact trigger coverage without checking. That's a Nina question and I'll get you a written answer.
[...]
[06:34] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Then let's do money now, because I don't want to spend twenty minutes falling in love with this.
[06:41] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Sensible. Growth starts at eighteen hundred a month, up to thirty users, on an annual agreement.
[...]
[07:09] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I could potentially do an annual prepay if that materially changes the number. Does it?
[07:16] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It can. I'd be lying if I said it halves it. It's a meaningful discount, not a transformation.
[...]
[08:15] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No. But you could count it for four weeks before you decide anything. That's free and it'd make the conversation much easier either way.
[...]
[09:25] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll take it.
[09:27] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): What about visibility of who owns what? Because the dead-employee problem is real.
[09:34] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Version history and change metadata on every workflow. So you can see what changed and when. And you'd typically define who can publish to production versus who can build in a dev workspace.
[09:49] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): We don't have a dev workspace. We don't have a dev anything.
[09:54] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] You'd get one. That's not extra cost, it's just how it's structured.
[10:00] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Do you do the AI stuff? Everyone does the AI stuff now.
[10:05] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): We do, but I'd underplay it for you. It's optional steps inside a workflow — classification, summarisation, extracting fields out of text, drafting something a human then approves. It's not an autonomous agent thing.
[10:22] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Is there something there for us or are you being polite?
[10:27] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): There might be one. You mentioned wanting a weekly digest of recurring support reasons pushed to the e-commerce and product teams?
[10:37] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): That was me. I want that. I've wanted that for two years.
[10:42] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a reasonable fit — summarise the week's tickets by theme, with links back to the underlying tickets so someone can check it.
[...]
[11:07] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Usage is scoped on workflow runs and premium connectors. I'd want to model that for your volumes rather than say "no" and surprise you later.
[...]
[11:47] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And eighteen hundred a month is —
[11:50] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Twenty-one, six. So it goes upstairs. Which is a different conversation and a slower one.
[...]
[12:12] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I'd like to clean up the automations before the holiday peak. Ideally something in place by early October, because after that nobody's changing anything until January.
[12:25] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Nobody touches anything in November. Company rule.
[12:29] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Sensible rule. So realistically a decision in — August?
[12:35] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): August, if we do it.
[...]
[14:48] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So — where does that leave you? Genuinely.
[14:53] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I like the monitoring. I like the reusable templates. That's the bit that speaks to our actual problem. I'm just not yet convinced the value closes the gap between this and the tools we already pay for.
[15:10] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a completely fair position.
[15:13] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I'm not saying no.
[15:16] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I know. And I'd rather have a considered maybe than an enthusiastic yes that dies in procurement.
[15:24] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): What would you want from us?
[15:27] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Two things, and both are cheap. One — Marcus logs the time spent on broken automations for four weeks. Not for me, for you. Two — send me your three worst automations, the ones that break most, and I'll come back with what they'd look like rebuilt here, plus an honest note on which bits are actually better and which are just different.
[15:53] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): You'll tell me which bits aren't better?
[15:56] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): If I don't, you'll find out in month two and then I've lost you anyway.
[16:02] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Alright. Marcus, can you do the logging thing?
[16:06] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): I can do the logging thing.
[16:09] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Then yes. Send me that.
[16:12] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll also get you written answers on the Shopify trigger coverage and the default processing region. Those are the two I dodged.
[...]
[16:39] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): God, no. Please don't. The pattern that works is picking the three that break most, moving those, running both for a bit, then deciding. Big-bang migrations of sixty automations is how these projects die.

=== CALL-004 (call kind: prospect)
CALL ID: CALL-004
DATE: 2026-06-18
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
PROSPECT: DeltaWorks Manufacturing
INDUSTRY: Industrial manufacturing
COMPANY SIZE: 4,500 employees
STAGE: Enterprise discovery
DURATION: 41 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Maya Chen, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Jon Bell, Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow
- Martin Vogel, Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing
- Anika Bose, IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing
TRANSCRIPT
[00:14] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): It's mostly right. I would change one thing. You have a product demonstration in the middle. I don't want that today.
[...]
[01:08] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then let's do governance and architecture first, current state woven through, and commercials at the end — and if we don't reach commercials, we don't reach commercials.
[...]
[04:14] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Yes, both available under the normal security process, along with SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA, and an architecture diagram.
[04:25] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Good. Send all of it. We will also send our questionnaire. It is two hundred and forty questions.
[...]
[04:36] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Everyone says that.
[04:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): We will complete it. If there are questions we can't answer we'll say "no" rather than "partially".
[...]
[05:53] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): That is the correct question and the answer is the second one, mostly. If the system records that a step took four days, that is process data. If the system reports that Herr Müller took four days, and that report goes to his manager, that is a different thing.
[06:14] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That's genuinely designable. You would aggregate at the queue or team level rather than the individual level, and you would restrict who can view run-level detail. It's a permissions and reporting design question.
[06:31] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): If you can show me that design, it helps my case with the works council considerably.
[06:38] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let's make that an explicit deliverable rather than a conversation. Jon, can you write a short note on team-level versus individual-level visibility?
[06:49] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Yes. And I'd want to be clear in it about what the platform records versus what it exposes, because those are different.
[07:00] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Yes. Exactly that distinction.
[07:04] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Can I add something here? This is the kind of thing that kills projects at DeltaWorks. Not the technology. [04:19] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): [laughs] It means procurement, yes.
[04:22] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Are you on a framework?
[04:24] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): We'd typically buy through one, yes. Anything over a threshold has to go through a compliant route.
[04:32] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What's the threshold?
[04:34] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): For services, it varies. Practically, anything meaningful goes through a framework or a tender, and a tender is nine months of my life.
[04:46] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then that's something we should establish early rather than in month four. I'd want to know which frameworks you use and whether we're on any of them, and if we're not, whether there's a compliant route at all.
[05:01] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): You're raising the procurement problem yourself.
[05:05] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather find out in week one that we can't be bought than in month six.
[05:11] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): That's — yes. Most vendors discover procurement in month six and are then very surprised about it.
[05:20] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I've been surprised about it.
[05:23] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): Everyone has.
[05:25] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Third thing, and this is the one I'd want you to hear. If your compliance process is genuinely manual and email-based, automating it will make it faster. But if the actual constraint is that you don't have enough electrical contractors, then a faster process just makes people wait more efficiently.
[05:47] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): [pause] That's a very good point and it's one I've made internally.
[05:53] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What's the answer?
[05:55] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): I think it's both. I think there's a genuine contractor capacity issue and I also think we lose days to nobody chasing. But I couldn't tell you the split, which is —
[06:09] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which is the same problem.
[06:11] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): Which is exactly the same problem, yes. I can't tell you the split because I don't have the data, and I don't have the data because nothing's instrumented.
[06:22] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then can I suggest something that isn't a sale?
[06:26] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): Go on.
[06:28] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): The first phase of something like this shouldn't be automating the voids process. It should be instrumenting it. Just recording state transitions — property became void, inspection booked, inspection done, works raised, works complete, compliance requested, certificate received, re-let. Timestamps only. No automation, no changing anyone's job.
[06:55] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): And then look at the data.
[06:58] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Run it for eight weeks and look at where the time actually goes. Then automate the two stages that turn out to matter, rather than the eight stages people complain about.
[07:11] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): That would be considerably cheaper.
[07:14] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's considerably cheaper and it's much easier to get through a procurement process, and if it turns out the answer is "you need more electricians", you've spent very little to find that out.
[07:28] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): You'd be arguing yourself down to a smaller deal.
[07:32] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd be arguing myself into a deal that survives. The ones that go wrong are the ones where we automate the wrong thing at scale.
[07:42] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): [pause] Alright. What do you want from me?
[07:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Half an hour, in the next couple of weeks, with you and whoever owns the housing management system technically. I'd want to understand the systems and I'd want to ask about procurement properly. No demo.
[08:03] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): No demo?
[08:05] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): If we get to a demo and it turns out we can't be procured or can't reach your housing system, I've wasted an hour of your life and mine.
[08:15] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): That's sensible. Our technical person is Priya Menon — she's our applications manager.
[08:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Would she come?
[08:25] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): If I ask her. She's sceptical of vendors, which I'd say is a feature.
[08:32] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's very much a feature. Ask her to bring the awkward questions.
[08:38] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): She won't need encouragement.
[08:41] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] Good. Anything I should send beforehand?
[08:46] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): Two things. What you'd need from our housing management system technically — Priya will want to know that before the call, not during it. And anything you've got on other housing associations or public sector bodies.
[09:02] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll be honest — I don't have a housing association reference. We have public sector customers but not in your sector.
[09:12] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): [pause] That's a problem for procurement rather than for me.
[09:17] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd assumed so. I'd rather say it now.
[09:21] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): Say it to Priya as well. She'll ask.
[09:25] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I will. What about frameworks — can you tell me which ones you use so I can check whether we're on them?
[09:33] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): I'll send you a list. There are three we use routinely.
[09:38] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then I'll check before we meet, and if we're not on any of them I'll tell you and we can decide whether it's worth continuing.
[09:47] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): You keep offering to end this.
[09:50] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather have five real conversations than twenty polite ones.
[09:55] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): [laughs] Alright. Send me the technical requirements, I'll send you the frameworks, and I'll get Priya. Week of the sixth?
[10:05] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Week of the sixth. Thank you, Ade. That was a much better cold call than I expected.
[10:12] Ade Balogun (Head of Business Change, Beacon Housing Trust): It was a much better cold call than I expected too. Bye.

=== CALL-020 (call kind: cold_call)
CALL ID: CALL-020
DATE: 2026-09-30
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
PROSPECT: Kestrel Robotics
INDUSTRY: Industrial robotics
COMPANY SIZE: 150 employees
STAGE: Cold call
DURATION: 8 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Leo Grant, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Rafael Santos, COO, Kestrel Robotics
TRANSCRIPT
[00:00] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Rafael.
[00:02] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Rafael, hi. Leo Grant, OrbitFlow. Cold call — I'll be quick and you can hang up.
[00:09] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] OrbitFlow. That's funny.
[00:13] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Is it?
[00:15] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): We're three weeks into evaluating Tray.io. Your name came up on a list and got crossed off.
[00:23] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Crossed off by whom?
[00:25] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Me. About a month ago.
[00:28] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask why? Genuinely — I'm not going to argue, I just want to know.
[00:34] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Your website. It's very enterprise. Governance, compliance, workspace separation. We're a hundred and fifty people building robots. I looked at it and thought, that's not for us.
[00:49] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [pause] That's a fair read of our website.
[00:53] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): You're agreeing?
[00:55] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Our marketing is aimed at companies with a governance function. You don't have one, so it isn't aimed at you.
[01:04] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): So why are you calling?
[01:06] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Because our marketing being aimed at somebody else doesn't mean the product is wrong for you. But I'd want to establish that in about four minutes rather than argue with your conclusion.
[01:19] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Go on then. Four minutes.
[01:22] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What are you trying to do with Tray?
[01:25] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Order-to-deployment. A customer orders a robot cell, and then there's engineering config, procurement of the long-lead parts, build scheduling, factory acceptance testing, shipping, and site commissioning. Seven stages, five systems, and about four months elapsed.
[01:47] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And what goes wrong?
[01:49] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Nothing goes wrong exactly. Things just take longer than they should because stage four doesn't know stage three finished until someone mentions it in a meeting.
[02:01] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): How much of the four months is waiting?
[02:04] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] I don't know. That's part of why we're doing this.
[02:10] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Okay. How's the Tray evaluation going?
[02:14] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Well. Genuinely well. Their team's been good.
[02:19] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then I'd say two things. First, I'm not going to tell you Tray is bad. It isn't. We lose to them and we beat them and it usually comes down to fit rather than quality.
[02:32] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): What's the second?
[02:34] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Three weeks in, with a decision coming, I'd be the third horse in a two-horse race, and that's usually a waste of everyone's time.
[02:44] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): You're talking yourself out of it again.
[02:47] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'm being realistic about it. Unless there's something in your evaluation that isn't going well, in which case I'd want to know what.
[02:57] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] There is one thing.
[03:00] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Go on.
[03:02] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Our ERP. It's a mid-market system, quite niche in manufacturing. Tray don't have a connector and we're looking at building against its API, which our one back-end developer estimates at three weeks.
[03:19] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Do you believe the estimate?
[03:21] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [laughs] No.
[03:23] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Nobody ever does.
[03:25] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): It'll be six.
[03:27] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd want to be honest — there's a good chance we don't have a connector either. What's the system?
[03:34] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): I'd rather not say on a cold call, if that's alright.
[03:39] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Completely fine. Then let me answer it generally. If it's a mid-market manufacturing ERP, we probably don't have a native connector, and you'd be building against the API with our generic REST action. Which is the same three weeks. Or six.
[03:57] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): So no advantage.
[04:00] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No advantage on that specific point, no. There might be one on what happens afterwards — who maintains it, whether it's reusable across the seven stages — but that's a subtler argument and I'm not going to pretend it's decisive.
[04:17] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): You keep doing this.
[04:19] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Doing what?
[04:21] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Conceding things.
[04:23] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather concede the things that are true and be believed on the things that aren't.
[04:29] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] Alright. What's the argument you would make?
[04:35] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Honestly, only one, and it's small. You said your one back-end developer would build the ERP integration. What happens when he's busy and someone in operations wants to change which stage triggers a notification?
[04:52] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): It waits.
[04:54] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): For how long?
[04:56] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] Depends. Weeks.
[04:59] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then the question for your evaluation — for either vendor — is whether the people who own the process can change the process without him. That's testable in a week and most evaluations don't test it.
[05:15] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): How would you test it?
[05:17] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Have someone in operations, not your developer, build one real workflow. Not with the developer sitting next to them. And see what happens.
[05:29] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] That's a good test.
[05:33] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's the test that predicts whether you're happy in two years. Run it against Tray — I mean that, run it against Tray, you're three weeks in and it costs you nothing.
[05:46] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): And if they pass?
[05:48] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then buy Tray. You'll have made a good decision for a good reason.
[05:54] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [laughs] You are the strangest salesperson I've spoken to this year.
[05:59] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll take that.
[06:01] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Look — I'm not going to restart the evaluation. We've got a decision date and I'm not moving it.
[06:09] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I wouldn't ask you to.
[06:11] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): But I'll do this. Send me something short — not a deck — on how you'd approach the seven-stage thing, and specifically on the operations-can-change-it question. If we go with Tray and it doesn't work out, I'll know who to call.
[06:29] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather have that than a demo you sit through politely.
[06:34] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): When's the decision?
[06:36] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Mid-October. Fourteenth, I think, or thereabouts.
[06:42] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Would it be worth a thirty-minute call before mid-October? Not a pitch. I'd walk through how I'd structure the seven stages and you can use the thinking whichever vendor you pick.
[06:56] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): You'd do that knowing we'll probably go with Tray?
[07:01] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): You're a hundred and fifty people building robots. You'll be four hundred people in three years and you'll be buying something else. I'd rather be the person who was useful.
[07:14] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] That's a long game.
[07:17] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's the only game in a market this small.
[07:21] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Alright. Send the note. If it's good I'll do the thirty minutes.
[07:27] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask one thing before you go?
[07:30] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Go on.
[07:32] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): The four months. Have you got a number for what a month costs you?
[07:37] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): A month of delay on a cell? Roughly, we recognise revenue on commissioning, so — a month is a month of revenue on a two hundred thousand pound order.
[07:50] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And how many orders in flight?
[07:53] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Eleven at the moment.
[07:55] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then if instrumenting the seven stages tells you where two weeks are going, that's a much bigger number than either vendor's licence.
[08:05] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] That's the slide I need for my board, isn't it.
[08:10] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's the slide you need regardless of who you buy from.
[08:14] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [laughs] Send the note, Leo.
[08:17] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I will. Thanks Rafael.
[08:20] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Bye.

answer.summary: Three cold calls produced a follow-up: CALL-016, CALL-017, CALL-018, and CALL-020 each ended with the prospect agreeing to a small next step; CALL-019 did not. CALL-019 is the exception because Yvonne explicitly said she would not read the email and did not want repeated follow-up.

answer.summary: Yes. The clearest inconsistency is on pricing terms: one OrbitFlow rep said Growth is on an annual agreement, while another said monthly billing is usually fine. There are also conflicting answers on identity/security features, integrations, and whether the product is fully no-code. The stronger-supported side is usually the more specific, later, or repeatedly stated answer from multiple reps in multiple calls.
